title: Efficient equations for VP with unrestricted complex coefficients
formal: For every fixed integer \(c\ge 1\), do there exist nonzero polynomials \(\mathrm{P}_{n}\) in \(N_{n}=\operatorname{binom}(n+n^{c},n)\) coefficient variables, with degree and algebraic circuit size at most \(C_{c} N_{n}^{a_{c}}\), such that for every fixed integer \(b\ge 1\) there is \(n_{0}(c,b)\) for which \(\mathrm{P}_{n}\)(\(coeff(f)\))=0 whenever \(n\ge n_{0}(c,b)\) and \(f\in \mathbb{C} [x_{1},\ldots ,x_{n}]\) has total degree at most \(n^{c}\) and an algebraic circuit of size at most \(n^{b}\)? Constants \(C_{c},a_{c}\) and the family \((\mathrm{P}_{n})\) may depend on c, but not on b. Coefficients of f may be arbitrary complex numbers. This expresses the source’s eventual vanishing on every polynomial-size family, without demanding a common finite threshold across all circuit-size exponents.
context:
The input to \(\mathrm{P}_{n}\) is the description of another polynomial by all its coefficients. An equation vanishes on easy polynomials and is nonzero somewhere else. Its efficiency is measured against this much larger coefficient-vector dimension.

The known positive result restricts the final polynomial’s coefficients, for example to \(\{- 1,0,1\}\). Its computing circuit may still use arbitrary complex constants internally. Removing that semantic restriction is the question here.

The source’s phrase “efficiently constructible equations” is formalized by membership in VP. The checked revision explicitly describes its upper-bound proofs as existential; the card therefore does not add a uniform circuit-generation algorithm.

Under sufficiently strong permanent hardness, the source rules out efficient equations for VNP over characteristic-zero fields. Since VP is a smaller class, an equation vanishing on VP need not vanish on VNP, so the theorem does not answer this card.

The February 2025 full version explicitly keeps Question 1.4 open while generalizing its positive and conditional negative results. The work was published in August 2026; the checked publisher abstract does not claim a resolution of unrestricted-coefficient VP.
why: Would clarify whether a broad family of algebraic lower-bound certificates can recognize all efficiently computable polynomials once arbitrary coefficients are allowed.
status_note: Checked the original question, complete February 2025 combined revision and August 2026 publisher record/abstract. No resolution of the unrestricted-complex-coefficient VP target was found through 12 September 2026. progress.text: Efficient equations are known for bounded-output-coefficient subclasses; the STACS paper gives a conditional obstruction for unrestricted-coefficient VNP while leaving VP open.
The combined full revision states the unrestricted VP problem as Question 1.4 and distinguishes it from its expanded positive and conditional results.
The combined work is published in computational complexity, volume 35, article 7.

definitions: An algebraic circuit over \(\mathbb{C}\) is a finite directed acyclic graph with inputs \(x_{1},\ldots ,x_{n}\) and arbitrary complex constants, binary addition and multiplication gates, and one output. Subtraction is allowed via multiplication by −1; there are no division gates. Its size is its number of vertices. It computes an exact formal polynomial, and each constant is one field element regardless of its bit description. \(VP_{\mathbb{C}}\) consists of polynomial families with polynomially bounded total degree and polynomially bounded nonuniform algebraic circuit size. For \(d=n^{c}\), list all monomials \(x_{1}^{\alpha _{1}}\cdots x_{n}^{\alpha _{n}}\) with \(\alpha _{i}\ge 0\) and \(\sum_{i}\alpha _{i}\le d\) in a fixed lexicographic order of exponent vectors. There are \(N_{n}=\operatorname{binom}(n+d,n)\) such monomials. \(coeff(f)\) is the full vector of their coefficients, including zeros. \(\mathrm{P}_{n}\) is a polynomial over \(\mathbb{C}\) whose variables are these \(N_{n}\) coordinates. Nonzero means not the zero formal polynomial; over \(\mathbb{C}\) it is equivalent to being nonzero at some coefficient vector. Both degree and circuit size of \(\mathrm{P}_{n}\) are bounded by a fixed polynomial in \(N_{n}\), not in n. The equations themselves are nonuniform: there is no additional requirement to construct their circuits in polynomial time from n. Vanishing must hold for all circuits under each fixed polynomial size bound eventually; the threshold can depend on that bound. Restricting c,b to positive integers covers arbitrary fixed polynomial exponents by increasing them. The statement imposes no bound on output coefficients of f or on constants used inside its circuit, and requests no explicit hard polynomial on which \(\mathrm{P}_{n}\) is nonzero.
answer_criterion: Prove existence of such a nontrivial polynomial-degree, polynomial-circuit-size family for every c, or refute the universal existence statement for at least one c. Vanishing only on polynomials with bounded integer coefficients, or only on a fixed restricted circuit architecture, does not establish the claim. Nonexistence of equations for VNP alone does not refute existence for VP.
